nodes.label: Resilience Alliance - Panarchy
nodes.summary: No system can be understood or managed by focusing on it at a single scale. All systems (and SESs especially) exist and function at multiple scales of space, time and social organisation, and the interactions across scales are fundamentally important in determining the dynamics of the system at any particular focal scale. This interacting set of hierarchically structured scales has been termed a "panarchy" (Gunderson and Holling 2003).
nodes.note: Panarchy relates to understanding regenerative systems as interdependent and co-existing systems which are constantly interacting with each other - a useful framework to consider when developing your own regenerative systems to question how they will impact adjacent context.

nodes.label: Ocean Archive
nodes.summary: Ocean-Archive.org is an online platform that investigates the potential of storytelling and transdisciplinary collaboration within and beyond archival practices. It strives to expand critical ocean literacy in a time of great necessity and catalyzes collective action for a living Ocean. The aim of Ocean-Archive.org is to bring together the multitude of voices and journeys around the Ocean and connect those striving to nurture and protect it. With ocean comm/uni/ty, the platform instigates conversations around the Ocean so that members can connect and co-create. Designed as a storytelling and pedagogical tool, Ocean-Archive.org translates current knowledge into a shared language that fosters synergy among art, science, policy, and conservation and enables us to make better decisions for urgently needed policies.
nodes.note: Culture is a vital part of understanding ourselves, our relationship with teh world and our relationship with a regenerative future.

nodes.label: A Textbook for the Ecocene
nodes.summary: A Textbook for the Ecocene is a how-to guide for connecting to self, community and planet. The Ecocene is an emergent and imagined geologic era where all humyns are living in reciprocity with their ecosystems again. Each textbook chapter shares practical exercises to try at home, Earth-centered theory and spirituality, and interviews with Black and Indigenous Earth warriors—cultural workers generating planetary liberation in their everyday lives.
nodes.note: It is a beautifully written discovery of connecting to self and to systems and communities around us. The format of a textbook makes it an accessible exploration of regenerative thinking.

nodes.label: CIVIC SQUARE BIRMINGHAM CIC
nodes.summary: CIVIC SQUARE's decade plan treats Birmingham neighbourhoods as units of change: co-built public square, regenerative economics lab, participatory creative ecosystem.
nodes.note: This project tests regenerative systems and principles at neighbourhood scale, prototyping a live project and learning from it, while setting long-term goals over the next decade.

nodes.label: Regenerative Design Lab - Constructivist
nodes.summary:
The Regenerative Design Lab is a highly influential think-tank and laboratory, bringining together leading built-environment professionals in the field of regenerative deisgn.

If you want to explore regenerative design at a deep level, or have a particular project in mind, then join the Regenerative Design Lab.
nodes.note: This has been the nexus for much of the thinking and writing around Regenerative Design in the Built Environment, including being the starting point for many recent influential books, and a host of important regenerative projects.

nodes.label: Keeping Up: Maintaining Biodiversity in Public Landscapes
nodes.summary: We can design as many biodiverse landscapes as we want, but their long-term success is dependent on the systems and people who maintain them. This report - an actionable guidebook - addresses critical knowledge gap between the design of biodiversity landscapes and the successful management and maintenance of these landscapes for long-term performance.
nodes.note: Maintenance teams can unlock our wildest dreams for biodiversity! They are a culturally and systemically underutilized group of experts who must be brought to design table. This report gives case studies, dialogues, and a sweeping catalog of actionable steps.

nodes.label: 3–30–300 Nature Recommendation
nodes.summary: In recent years, the time modern people spend in nature has decreased due to urbanization and cultural changes. This affects not only our well-being and health but also our relationship with the nature around us. The 3–30–300 Nature Recommendation guides us back to natural environments.
nodes.note: Strengthening people's connection to nature creates opportunities for a broader shift in our relationship with the natural world. One way to strengthen this connection is to increase the time spent in natural environments. The "3–30–300 Nature Recommendation" offers recommendations and reasoning for increasing time spent in nature.

nodes.label: Transformative action towards regenerative food systems: A large-scale case study
nodes.authors: Sam J. Buckton, Ioan Fazey, Bob Doherty, Maria Bryant, Steven A. Banwart, Esther Carmen, Annie Connolly, Katherine Denby, Ian Kendrick, Bill Sharpe, Ruth N. Wade, Peter Ball, Sarah Bridle, Grace Gardner, Anthonia James, Belinda Morris, Sophie Stewart, Myles Bremner, Pippa J. Chapman, Juan Pablo Cord
nodes.summary: The paper identifies and discusses six actions that need to be taken to achieve transformational, systems-level change towards a regenerative food system.

nodes.label: An essay to expand Ecosystemic Design with the interconnection between Unlearning, Grief and Utupia * Journal of Futures Studies
nodes.summary: The essay presents a possible path towards regenerated futures. It argues that we are undergoing a large process of unlearning that reaches the depth of our psyche and that, for us to imagine and create regenerated realities we need to undergo a process of grief — grieving the loss of our identity, references and values. With unlearning and grieving, we can foster utupian (a decolonial vew of utopia) visions and futures.
nodes.note: This is a contribution to think of regeneration from a decolonial persepctive, tackling a rather overlooked aspect of regeneration which is its subjective side. Thinking of unlearning, grieving and imagining utopias (utupias) as connected processes might help us move towards regenerated futures/realities with more ease.

nodes.label: Regenerative Design and Craft Lab
nodes.summary: How could local crops and crafts help bring regional regeneration? To address this question, this project proposes the co-creation of a Regenerative Design and Craft Lab, promoting research approaches that are regionally situated and ecologically aware and that combine traditional craft with future-oriented design.
nodes.note: The pilot activities funded by the University of Warwick Interdisciplinary Research Development Award will seed the idea of a Regenerative Design and Craft Lab at Warwick - a digitally augmented 21st Century ‘cottage industry’. Dedicated to imagining the design and crafts of the future as localised regenerative practices rooted in local resources and a restorative history of the bioregion, the Lab will also be wired into a growing global community of like-minded researchers.

nodes.label: Future Build: How Construction Can Heal Our Planet
nodes.summary: Narrative non-fiction book (for lay reader) building knowledge up from material impacts, through design, and onto purpose, usefulness, change making and Regenerative Design. More info and reviews (inc Jo da Silva) at futurebuildbook.com
nodes.note: You can use this to help a client or collaborator to understand how buildings can do more good.

nodes.label: Regenerative design - towards living in harmony with nature
nodes.summary: A report outlining regenerative principles applying to the built environment industry. It contains definitions, case studies and framing of how regenerative design might be applied to understanding the systems within which the industry operates.
nodes.note: A comprehensive study of regenerative design in the built environment context.

nodes.label: Architects Climate Action Network
nodes.summary: Organising within the architecture profession — retrofit-first campaigning, embodied carbon regulation, and the argument for building less.

nodes.label: RMI
nodes.summary: Independent research on energy transition, from deep retrofit economics to embodied carbon in construction materials.

nodes.label: Passivhaus Trust
nodes.summary: The UK body for the Passivhaus standard — fabric-first energy performance verified by measurement rather than modelled intent.

nodes.label: New European Bauhaus
nodes.summary: The EU's attempt to bind the Green Deal to beauty, sustainability and community — and a live argument about whether aesthetics belong in climate policy.

nodes.label: Rewilding Britain
nodes.summary: Case studies and evidence for letting land recover its own processes, at the scale where ecological function actually returns.

nodes.label: Braiding Sweetgrass
nodes.summary: Indigenous knowledge and plant science held together. The honourable harvest as a working ethic for taking anything from a living system.

nodes.label: Pattern Language and The Nature of Order
nodes.summary: Alexander's argument that living structure emerges from repeated, named, locally-adapted moves — the ancestor of most attempts to write design knowledge down.

nodes.label: One Planet Living
nodes.summary: Ten principles for living within one planet's resources, developed through BedZED and used since as a masterplanning framework.

nodes.label: Global Footprint Network
nodes.summary: Ecological footprint and biocapacity accounts by country — the source behind Earth Overshoot Day and most one-planet framings.

nodes.label: Project Drawdown Solutions
nodes.summary: Climate solutions ranked by modelled emissions impact, with the assumptions published — useful precisely because it lets you argue with the ranking.

nodes.label: Material Cultures
nodes.summary: Research and practice rebuilding a construction culture around bio-based materials grown in the landscapes that surround a site — straw, hemp, timber, earth.

nodes.label: Circularity Gap Report
nodes.summary: An annual measurement of what share of the global economy is actually circular.

nodes.label: Buildings As Material Banks
nodes.summary: The project that developed material passports and reversible building design — treating a building as a temporary arrangement of materials that must be recoverable.

nodes.label: UK Green Building Council
nodes.summary: Home of the UK Net Zero Carbon Buildings Framework and the whole-life carbon roadmap for the sector.

nodes.label: LETI
nodes.summary: Volunteer-built guidance, the Climate Emergency Design Guide and the Embodied Carbon Primer, that turned UK net-zero targets into numbers a design team can work to.

nodes.label: RIBA 2030 Climate Challenge
nodes.summary: Stepped targets to 2030 for operational energy, embodied carbon and potable water, given per square metre so projects can be held to them.

nodes.label: Carbon Leadership Forum
nodes.summary: Open research and open data on embodied carbon, including the EC3 tool and the material baselines most whole-life assessments are compared against.

nodes.label: 14 Patterns of Biophilic Design
nodes.authors: William Browning, Catherine Ryan, Joseph Clancy
nodes.summary: Fourteen named, evidenced patterns for putting nature into buildings, each with the health outcome it is associated with.

nodes.label: Cradle to Cradle Certified
nodes.authors: Cradle to Cradle Products Innovation Institute
nodes.summary: Product standard built on McDonough and Braungart's argument that waste is a design error — material health, circularity, clean air, water, social fairness.

nodes.label: Living Building Challenge
nodes.summary: A certification organised as seven petals and judged on measured performance over twelve months of occupation, not on prediction.

nodes.label: Biomimicry 3.8
nodes.summary: Consultancy behind Ecological Performance Standards, which set a project's targets from what the intact local ecosystem would do on that same ground.

nodes.label: AskNature
nodes.summary: A searchable library of biological strategies indexed by the design function they address — how does nature manage water, resist fracture, cool itself.

nodes.label: Planetary Boundaries
nodes.authors: Johan Rockström, Will Steffen and colleagues
nodes.summary: Definition of the nine processes that regulate the stability of the Earth systems, and how far we have already transgressed several of them. The ceiling that regenerative targets are measured against.

nodes.label: Doughnut Economics Action Lab
nodes.summary: Tools for working between the social foundation and the ecological ceiling, including the city portrait method used to downscale planetary boundaries to a place.

nodes.label: Circular Economy Introduction
nodes.summary: The butterfly diagram and the three principles — eliminate waste, circulate materials, regenerate nature. One of the most-borrowed diagrams in the field.

nodes.label: Regenesis Group
nodes.authors: Pamela Mang, Bill Reed, Ben Haggard
nodes.summary: The practice that developed story-of-place as a working method: read the living system of a site before proposing anything, and design so the place can keep evolving.

nodes.label: Shifting from 'sustainability' to regeneration
nodes.summary: The paper that drew the trajectory from degenerative through neutral to regenerative practice, and argued that doing less harm is not a destination.

nodes.label: Leverage Points: Places to Intervene in a System
nodes.summary: Useful framing for regenerative design which considers how to understand and intervene in complex systems. It describes twelve places to intervene in a system — the foundational text for why regenerative work is rarely a technical problem but a systems problem.

sources.title: Regenerative Design and Craft Lab
sources.summary: How could local crops and crafts help bring regional regeneration? To address this question, this project proposes the co-creation of a Regenerative Design and Craft Lab, promoting research approaches that are regionally situated and ecologically aware and that combine traditional craft with future-oriented design.
sources.note: The pilot activities funded by the University of Warwick Interdisciplinary Research Development Award will seed the idea of a Regenerative Design and Craft Lab at Warwick - a digitally augmented 21st Century ‘cottage industry’. Dedicated to imagining the design and crafts of the future as localised regenerative practices rooted in local resources and a restorative history of the bioregion, the Lab will also be wired into a growing global community of like-minded researchers.

sources.title: Future Build: How Construction Can Heal Our Planet
sources.summary: Narrative non-fiction book (for lay reader) building knowledge up from material impacts, through design, and onto purpose, usefulness, change making and Regenerative Design. More info and reviews (inc Jo da Silva) at futurebuildbook.com
sources.note: You can use this to help a client or collaborator to understand how buildings can do more good.

sources.title: Regenerative design - towards living in harmony with nature
sources.summary: A report outlining regenerative principles applying to the built environment industry. It contains definitions, case studies and framing of how regenerative design might be applied to understanding the systems within which the industry operates.
sources.note: A comprehensive study of regenerative design in the built environment context.

sources.title: Architects Climate Action Network
sources.summary: Organising within the architecture profession — retrofit-first campaigning, embodied carbon regulation, and the argument for building less.

sources.title: RMI
sources.summary: Independent research on energy transition, from deep retrofit economics to embodied carbon in construction materials.

sources.title: Passivhaus Trust
sources.summary: The UK body for the Passivhaus standard — fabric-first energy performance verified by measurement rather than modelled intent.

sources.title: New European Bauhaus
sources.summary: The EU's attempt to bind the Green Deal to beauty, sustainability and community — and a live argument about whether aesthetics belong in climate policy.

sources.title: Rewilding Britain
sources.summary: Case studies and evidence for letting land recover its own processes, at the scale where ecological function actually returns.

sources.title: Braiding Sweetgrass
sources.summary: Indigenous knowledge and plant science held together. The honourable harvest as a working ethic for taking anything from a living system.

sources.title: Pattern Language and The Nature of Order
sources.summary: Alexander's argument that living structure emerges from repeated, named, locally-adapted moves — the ancestor of most attempts to write design knowledge down.

sources.title: One Planet Living
sources.summary: Ten principles for living within one planet's resources, developed through BedZED and used since as a masterplanning framework.

sources.title: Global Footprint Network
sources.summary: Ecological footprint and biocapacity accounts by country — the source behind Earth Overshoot Day and most one-planet framings.

sources.title: Project Drawdown Solutions
sources.summary: Climate solutions ranked by modelled emissions impact, with the assumptions published — useful precisely because it lets you argue with the ranking.

sources.title: Material Cultures
sources.summary: Research and practice rebuilding a construction culture around bio-based materials grown in the landscapes that surround a site — straw, hemp, timber, earth.

sources.title: Circularity Gap Report
sources.summary: An annual measurement of what share of the global economy is actually circular.

sources.title: Buildings As Material Banks
sources.summary: The project that developed material passports and reversible building design — treating a building as a temporary arrangement of materials that must be recoverable.

sources.title: UK Green Building Council
sources.summary: Home of the UK Net Zero Carbon Buildings Framework and the whole-life carbon roadmap for the sector.

sources.title: LETI
sources.summary: Volunteer-built guidance, the Climate Emergency Design Guide and the Embodied Carbon Primer, that turned UK net-zero targets into numbers a design team can work to.

sources.title: RIBA 2030 Climate Challenge
sources.summary: Stepped targets to 2030 for operational energy, embodied carbon and potable water, given per square metre so projects can be held to them.

sources.title: Carbon Leadership Forum
sources.summary: Open research and open data on embodied carbon, including the EC3 tool and the material baselines most whole-life assessments are compared against.

sources.title: 14 Patterns of Biophilic Design
sources.authors: William Browning, Catherine Ryan, Joseph Clancy
sources.summary: Fourteen named, evidenced patterns for putting nature into buildings, each with the health outcome it is associated with.

sources.title: Cradle to Cradle Certified
sources.authors: Cradle to Cradle Products Innovation Institute
sources.summary: Product standard built on McDonough and Braungart's argument that waste is a design error — material health, circularity, clean air, water, social fairness.

sources.title: Living Building Challenge
sources.summary: A certification organised as seven petals and judged on measured performance over twelve months of occupation, not on prediction.

sources.title: Biomimicry 3.8
sources.summary: Consultancy behind Ecological Performance Standards, which set a project's targets from what the intact local ecosystem would do on that same ground.

sources.title: AskNature
sources.summary: A searchable library of biological strategies indexed by the design function they address — how does nature manage water, resist fracture, cool itself.

sources.title: Planetary Boundaries
sources.authors: Johan Rockström, Will Steffen and colleagues
sources.summary: Definition of the nine processes that regulate the stability of the Earth systems, and how far we have already transgressed several of them. The ceiling that regenerative targets are measured against.

sources.title: Doughnut Economics Action Lab
sources.summary: Tools for working between the social foundation and the ecological ceiling, including the city portrait method used to downscale planetary boundaries to a place.

sources.title: Circular Economy Introduction
sources.summary: The butterfly diagram and the three principles — eliminate waste, circulate materials, regenerate nature. One of the most-borrowed diagrams in the field.

sources.title: Regenesis Group
sources.authors: Pamela Mang, Bill Reed, Ben Haggard
sources.summary: The practice that developed story-of-place as a working method: read the living system of a site before proposing anything, and design so the place can keep evolving.

sources.title: Shifting from 'sustainability' to regeneration
sources.summary: The paper that drew the trajectory from degenerative through neutral to regenerative practice, and argued that doing less harm is not a destination.

sources.title: Leverage Points: Places to Intervene in a System
sources.summary: Useful framing for regenerative design which considers how to understand and intervene in complex systems. It describes twelve places to intervene in a system — the foundational text for why regenerative work is rarely a technical problem but a systems problem.
